_comentario: Checklists by area for go-expert. 'origem': 'from source' (the cited page says so; the 'terms' are checked by tests/verify_citations.py), 'inference' (conclusion of the package from the sources) or 'extrapolation' (knowledge outside the sources). Pages = PDF (Little: printed = N-1). [DATED] items come from Eff (2009) or Little (go1.3.3). Area keys are kept in Portuguese (go_checklist.py also accepts English aliases).

itens.texto: Let gofmt decide the layout (do not align comments or fields by hand)
terms: Gofmt will do that for you

itens.texto: Indent with tabs
Opening brace on the same line as if/for/switch/select
No parentheses in if/for/switch
terms: do not have parentheses in their syntax

itens.texto: Doc comment conventions beyond the basics: not covered (Effective Go refers to 'Go Doc Comments', which is not in the sources)
Package name in lowercase, one word, no underscore or mixedCaps
terms: no need for underscores or mixedCaps

itens.texto: Do not repeat the package name in the symbol (bufio.Reader, not BufReader; ring.New, not NewRing)
Getter without Get (Owner, not GetOwner); setter SetOwner
One-method interface: method name + -er
Visibility by initial uppercase letter (types, functions and fields)
Handle every error return before using the result; do not discard it with _ to 'ignore' it
Return early on the error path, without an unnecessary else
defer resource.Close() right after checking the open error
Sentinel such as io.EOF: compare with ==
A structured error (like os.PathError) lets you inspect the cause by type switch/assertion
Error chaining (%w, errors.Is/As): the sources only cite errors.Join and multiple %w (RN1.20 p.6, p.10); any guidance beyond that is [extrapolation]
Pointer receiver when the method needs to change the receiver
terms: pointer methods can modify the receiver

itens.texto: A pointer method only on a pointer (an addressable value gets & automatically); only *T satisfies the interface with pointer methods
If you need to print T and *T with String(), the String receiver must be a value
terms: receiver for String must be of

itens.texto: [DATED] Little's heuristic: when in doubt, use a pointer (the author's opinion, not a Spec rule)
terms: if you aren't sure, use a pointer

itens.texto: Mixing value and pointer receivers on the same type: no source covers it; avoid it without a reason because of the method set rule
Reassign the result of append (the underlying array may change)
make([]T, n) creates n elements; for capacity without elements use make([]T, 0, n)
terms: length of 0 but with a capacity of 10

itens.texto: A subslice shares the array (the upper bound of slicing is cap); use copy or the a[low:high:max] form to isolate
Nil map: writing panics (initialize with make)
terms: Assigning to an element of a nil map causes a run-time panic

itens.texto: Do not depend on map iteration order
A slice cannot be a map key (equality is not defined)
terms: Slices cannot be used as map keys

itens.texto: Accept the narrow interface the function actually uses (e.g. io.Closer)
Single-form type assertion only if a crash is acceptable; otherwise use comma ok
String() must not format its own type with %s/%v (recursion); convert to the base type
An interface holding a nil pointer is not nil: deduction from Spec p.12 + p.69; no source describes the trap
'Accept interfaces, return structs' is not in any source; if you recommend it, label it
defer in a loop only runs at the end of the function (deferred calls run before the function returns)
defer arguments are evaluated when the defer is executed; a nil function panics only at invocation
terms: not when the "defer" statement is executed

itens.texto: panic only for the 'impossible' or initialization failure; libraries avoid panic
terms: real library functions should avoid panic

itens.texto: recover only works when called directly by a deferred function
terms: called directly by a deferred function

itens.texto: Convert an internal panic into an error at the package boundary (local error type, re-panic if it is another)
terms: calling panic with a local error type

itens.texto: panic(nil) becomes *runtime.PanicNilError since Go 1.21 (panicnil=1 reverts)
time.Sleep is not synchronization (Little uses it only to show that main exits without waiting)
terms: this is bad, don't do this!

itens.texto: Lock() followed by defer Unlock(); forgetting Unlock causes deadlock
When main returns the program exits and does not wait for the other goroutines
terms: It does not wait for other

itens.texto: Goroutine in a loop: before Go 1.22 the loop variable is shared; find out the version (that it depends on the go line of go.mod is an inference)
Limit goroutine creation (buffered channel as a semaphore or a fixed pool)
Go 1.23+: Timer/Ticker channel is unbuffered; len(t.C) is not a readiness test
select with default in a loop, with no other blocking, spins without waiting (burns CPU)
Who closes the channel: the Spec does not say; 'the sender closes' is an inference (sending on a closed channel panics, Spec p.80)
sync.WaitGroup, context and errgroup: not covered in the sources; any recommended use is [extrapolation]
~T requires the underlying type of T to be T and T not to be an interface (~MyInt is illegal)
Non-interface terms of a union must be disjoint (~int | MyInt is illegal)
Interfaces satisfy comparable since Go 1.20 (any works in [K comparable]) with a panic risk when comparing
A partial list of type arguments is a prefix; apply[] is illegal; with no argument that fixes the parameter, pass the type argument explicitly
A method only uses the receiver's type parameters (there is no method with its own type parameters)
Check the version required by the feature (Spec version table)
terms: will be rejected if the implied or required language version

itens.texto: When to use generics: no source gives guidance; any recommendation is [extrapolation]
Read the go line and the toolchain directive of go.mod; raising only the toolchain preserves the old behavior of the go line
terms: preserves the behavior of the older toolchain

itens.texto: rand.Seed: global generator seeded automatically in 1.20; top-level Seed becomes a no-op in 1.24 (randseednop=0 reverts)
Go 1.24: the tool directive in go.mod replaces the tools.go pattern
Raising one version at a time is an inference (the notes do not dictate the order)
Go 1.25 and 1.26: no release notes in the sources; say there is no coverage
